basis: Constitutional trisomy 8 causes characteristic skeletal and developmental abnormalities; congenital renal abnormalities occur in roughly 30-50%. Malignancy risk excluded.

decisions.renal: involved: congenital renal malformations affect roughly 30-50% of constitutional cases.

basis: Postinfectious scarring narrows the urethra; the residual structural disorder does not establish active infection or immune-mediated disease.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: postinfectious urethral scarring is a sequela; ongoing infection is not required.

basis: Defining developmental, skeletal and hair/nail abnormalities; hearing impairment 3/4 (75%). Visual impairment 2/3 and cleft palate 2/4 omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.ocular: none under cap: visual impairment affects 2/3; retain defining axes and hearing impairment, reported in 3/4.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: characteristic sparse scalp hair and abnormal hair distribution form part of the defining Coffin-Siris phenotype.

basis: Craniosynostosis and polysyndactyly define Carpenter syndrome; intellectual disability affects roughly half or more. Cardiac defects are around 20-30% in RAB23-related cases.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: cardiac defects occur in approximately 20-30% of RAB23-related cases; evidence does not securely establish the threshold.
decisions.neurologic: involved: intellectual disability affects roughly half or more; it is variable rather than a defining skeletal criterion.

basis: Lipoprotein disorder defined by malabsorption and neurologic dysfunction; progressive visual loss occurs in 30-79%. Anemia in 30-79% omitted at cap; hepatic injury uncommon.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: intestinal fat malabsorption is an explicit defining manifestation, present in 80-99%.
decisions.neurologic: primary: neurologic dysfunction is explicit in the definition and disease ancestry; nervous-system abnormalities occur in 80-99%.

basis: Odontogenic epithelial tumour; the solid/multicystic form occupies and destructively expands jawbone in most patients.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: jawbone occupation and destruction occur in most solid/multicystic lesions; the tumour originates in odontogenic epithelium.

basis: Motor axonal neuropathy occurs in 7/7 patients; muscle wasting and weakness reflect denervation without evidence of intrinsic muscle disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: weakness and amyotrophy in 7/7 are consequences of motor denervation, without direct skeletal muscle pathology.

basis: Neurogenic scapuloperoneal disorder with intrinsic myofibrillar pathology: rimmed vacuoles in 6/8 and shoulder atrophy in 13/15. Dysphagia affects only 2/15.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: myofibrillar disease ancestry and intrinsic muscle pathology, including rimmed vacuoles in 6/8, establish muscle as a defining site.

basis: CD40L immunodeficiency; intrinsic neutropenia in 39/62 (63%) and oral ulceration in 25/56 (45%). Separately diagnosed infections excluded; cholangitis occurs in 20%.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: recurrent oral ulceration represents mucosal breakdown in 25/56 (45%), associated with intrinsic neutropenia; mouth belongs to this axis.

basis: Dermal elastin loss defines disease; joint laxity, hyperlordosis and tibial abnormalities occur in 30-79%. Irregular dentition and high palate do not establish oral functional damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: irregular dentition and high palate occur in 30-79%, but these annotations alone do not establish destructive or functionally damaging oral disease.
